summary.title: Improving direct-mapped cache performance by the addition of a small fully-associative cache and prefetch buffers
summary.one_liner: Learn how miss caches, victim caches, and stream buffers (including multiway stream buffers) reduce direct-mapped cache conflict, capacity, and compulsory misses.
keywords: small associative cache next to direct-mapped cache
takeaways: A miss cache is a small fully-associative cache between a cache and its refill path, giving a 1-cycle miss penalty for misses that hit in it.
Small miss caches of 2 to 5 entries are shown to be very effective at removing mapping conflict misses in first-level direct-mapped caches.
A victim cache loads the small fully-associative cache with the victim of a miss rather than the requested line, and 1 to 5 entries removes conflict misses even better than miss caching.
Stream buffers prefetch lines starting at a miss address and place them in the buffer rather than the cache; they remove capacity and compulsory misses and some instruction cache conflict misses.
A multiway stream buffer is an extension of the basic stream buffer introduced in this paper.
summary.summary: This IEEE conference paper presents hardware techniques for improving first-level cache performance. It describes miss caching, where a small fully-associative cache sits between a cache and its refill path, and victim caching, which fills that small cache with evicted victims instead of requested lines. It also introduces stream buffers that prefetch sequential lines from a miss address into a separate buffer, plus an extension called the multiway stream buffer. The paper reports that small structures of a few entries are effective at removing conflict, capacity, and compulsory misses. The page text is the abstract only, so details of the evaluation are not available here.
